subject: Data sunset timeline and log eviction exception — Asteria Health
messages:
From: Lina Morales <lina.morales@asteriahealth.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@asteriahealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary log hold & extended backup window for upcoming audit

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this — Asteria has a regulatory audit scheduled for Feb and our compliance team is asking for a temporary extension to certain retention windows while evidence collection is in progress. Specifically: 

- Keep application logs for 18 months (current agreement: 6 months) for a cohort of healthcare tenant IDs (we can provide the tenant list).
- Delay deletion of nightly backup snapshots for a 120-day supplemental hold before automatic pruning.

We understand this is an exception to your standard purge cadence. We need:
1) A concise statement of what Redwood can commit to (timelines, scope, and any impact on unit costs).
2) A technical description we can include in our audit package that explains how logs/backups will be isolated and later removed.
3) Any security controls or additional safeguards you require from our side (e.g., access logs, IP allowlist for retrieval).

Attaching the audit requirements checklist. Procurement is looped in for contract addenda. Can we aim for a proposal by EOD Wednesday?

Best,
Lina Morales
Senior Compliance Manager
Asteria Health
[attachment: Asteria_Audit_Checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lina Morales <lina.morales@asteriahealth.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary log hold & extended backup window for upcoming audit

Lina — thanks for the clear ask and the checklist. We can accommodate a scoped exception but need to lock down specifics so we can (a) scope the operational changes, (b) quantify cost delta, and (c) limit blast radius. Proposal below.

Summary proposal (subject to sign-off by Legal & Ops):
- Logs: 18 months TTL for listed tenant IDs only. All other tenants remain at standard 180 days.
- Backups: 120-day supplemental hold applied to immutable nightly snapshots for the specified tenant list; snapshots will be tagged and stored in a segregated retention bucket.
- Implementation timeframe: 5 business days after agreement signature to apply tagging + routing rules; full enforcement/testing in 10 business days.
- Cost: incremental storage and snapshot-retention fees (we’ll share an estimate after Ops calculates expected snapshot volume).

Requirements from Asteria:
- Final tenant ID list in CSV format.
- Point of contact for retrieval requests with documented justification.
- Signed addendum (we can provide a template).

We will:
- Provide a short technical memo (one page) for your audit package detailing retention exception controls and deletion rollback steps.
- Add audit logging for all retrieval/restore events and provide a one-time export of access logs for the exception window.

I’ve asked Aditya to draft the technical implementation notes and Kim to review from Legal. If this looks directionally right we’ll produce the addendum and a one-page memo.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | support@redwoodinference.com

Grace — this is exactly the kind of summary our auditors want. Attaching our SOC2 scoping memo and the tentative tenant list (redacted). Procurement confirms they can sign an addendum but need Redwood’s standard language and a final cost estimate.

Notes from Security team:

- Prefer read-only retrieval channels and ephemeral export tokens where possible.

Can you also confirm retention-of-backup-region? We need to ensure data doesn’t cross into non-US storage for this cohort.

Thanks,
Lina
Senior Compliance Manager
Asteria Health

From: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com, lina.morales@asteriahealth.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary log hold & extended backup window for upcoming audit

Lina / Grace — technical details and ops plan below. I’ve assumed the tenant list is <100 tenants; if larger we’ll need to re-run the cost calc.

What we will implement:
- Tagging: On addendum effective date we’ll apply a retention tag (asteria-audit-hold-2026) to all nightly snapshots for the provided tenant IDs. Tags route to a segregated S3-compatible bucket with an explicit policy preventing TTL-driven prune jobs from touching objects with that tag.
- Backup hold: Prune job will skip tagged snapshots for 120 days. After 120 days snapshots will re-enter the normal lifecycle and be eligible for pruning.
- Logs: We’ll extend TTL to 18 months for logs scoped to tenant IDs by applying tenant-scoped log-index aliasing and changing the TTL config for that alias only. No change to global TTL.
- Cross-border controls: We will pin storage for the tagged bucket to US regions only (us-west-2 by default); no automatic replication will occur for these objects.
- Access & audit: Retrieval requests create a ticket in our internal ticketing system; retrieval requires two approvals (Redwood comms+customer requestor) and every retrieval is logged and exported monthly as CSV to the shared drive link below.

Operational timeline:
- Day 0: Sign addendum + tenant CSV delivered.
- Day 1–3: Ops applies tagging policy and validates bucket policies.
- Day 4–7: Run a pilot on 3 tenants and validate that prune jobs skip tagged objects and log TTL updated.
- Day 8–10: Full rollout across supplied tenants.

Risks / caveats:
- Cost delta: dependent on snapshot counts and log ingestion; estimate to follow (we’ll present a per-tenant and aggregate number).
- Immutable snapshot storage still counts toward customer storage quotas and may affect billing if volume is large.
- Forensic export: large exports might require short-lived elevated network egress; network costs would be billed separately unless included in addendum.

I’ve attached a short ops runbook stub for your review.

—Aditya Rao
Director, Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference
[attachment: ops-runbook-asteria-hold.txt (text)]

From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, procurement@asteriahealth.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 16:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary log hold & extended backup window for upcoming audit

Lina / team — Legal has reviewed and can approve a scoped addendum with the following constraints (summarized):

- Scope limited to the tenant IDs provided in the CSV; any additional tenants require a separate addendum.
- Exception period capped at 270 days total; individual snapshot holds may not exceed 120 days beyond normal retention without further approval.
- Redwood will provide monthly access log exports as described by Aditya. Logs will include actor, timestamp, and justification.
- Data residency: we confirm pinned storage to US-only regions for the tagged objects; this will be reflected in the addendum.
- Cost/chargebacks: incremental storage and egress are billable to the customer and will appear on the invoice as a line item referencing the addendum.

Action items:
1) Asteria — please deliver the tenant CSV and procurement contact.
2) Redwood — we will prepare the addendum (Grace) and the technical memo for audit (Aditya) by EOD Wednesday.
3) Procurement — prepare a countersigned DocuSign link after we share the addendum.

Once we have the tenant list and procurement contact I’ll run a quick legal review to ensure the language aligns with our DPA and subprocessor obligations.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
